opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047), full-time Payroll Specialist, requests admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max at write unless their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the max is read. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requests admin on Source Code. Admin is only allowed for full-time employees whose role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer role does), so admin is not permitted. Per HR records, E047 is full-time, so the maximum allowed level is write. Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: write. (Note: the Security note lists E047 as a contractor with basic training, which would cap at read; I am relying on the employment record that is authoritative for employment type, but either way admin is denied.)
